challenges.title: Ordering ramen
challenges.context: You sit down at a small ramen shop. The staff member comes over.

steps.speaker: hiro
steps.text: いらっしゃいませ！ご{注文|ちゅうもん}は？

choices.text: しょうゆラーメンをひとつお{願|ねが}いします。
choices.feedback: Item + number + お願いします. That's how orders are made.
choices.why: 〜をひとつお願いします is the standard polite order. ひとつ, ふたつ… count most things.

choices.text: しょうゆラーメンをひとつ{食|た}べます。
choices.translation: I will eat one shoyu ramen.
choices.feedback: 食べます = 'I'll eat'. To order, use 〜をお願いします or 〜をください.
choices.why: Ordering is a request, so use お願いします／ください rather than a statement about yourself.

choices.text: ラーメンはどこですか？
choices.feedback: You're IN the ramen shop! Just order: 〜をお願いします.
choices.why: どこですか asks for a location. For orders, name the dish + お願いします.

steps.speaker: hiro
steps.text: お{飲|の}み{物|もの}はいかがですか？
steps.translation: Would you like something to drink?

choices.text: いえ、{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です。
choices.feedback: A soft, polite 'no thanks'.
choices.why: いかがですか offers something. 大丈夫です declines gently, or accept with はい、〜をお願いします.

choices.text: はい、いかがです。
choices.feedback: いかが means 'how about…?'. You can't answer with it.
choices.why: Answer offers with お願いします (yes) or 大丈夫です (no thanks).

choices.text: {飲|の}み{物|もの}、いらない。
choices.feedback: Understandable, but blunt and casual for a restaurant.
choices.why: いらない is plain-form 'don't need'. With staff, 大丈夫です sounds much softer.

challenges.title: Lost in the neighbourhood
challenges.context: You're looking at a map on your phone. An older man stops beside you.

steps.speaker: ojisan
steps.text: どうしましたか？{道|みち}に{迷|まよ}いましたか？
steps.reading: Dou shimashita ka? Michi ni mayoimashita ka?

choices.text: はい。すみません、{駅|えき}はどちらですか？
choices.reading: Hai. Sumimasen, eki wa dochira desu ka?
choices.translation: Yes. Excuse me, which way is the station?
choices.feedback: どちら is the polite version of どこ. Perfect with an older stranger.
choices.why: どちら (which way / where) is softer and more polite than どこ, so it's great with elders and strangers.

choices.text: はい、{迷|まよ}いました。さようなら。
choices.feedback: You admitted you're lost, then left before he could help!
choices.why: After accepting help, ask your actual question. さようなら ends the conversation.

choices.text: いいえ、{駅|えき}です。
choices.feedback: That doesn't answer his question or ask for directions.
choices.why: 迷いましたか？ is a yes/no question. Answer はい, then ask 〜はどちらですか？

challenges.title: Late for class
challenges.context: You rush into Japanese class five minutes late.

steps.speaker: sensei
steps.text: {遅|おそ}かったですね。どうしましたか？
steps.reading: Osokatta desu ne. Dou shimashita ka?

choices.text: {遅|おく}れてすみません。{電車|でんしゃ}が{遅|おく}れました。
choices.translation: Sorry I'm late. The train was delayed.
choices.feedback: Apology first, then the reason. Very natural.
choices.why: 〜てすみません = 'sorry for ~ing'. 遅れる (to be late) is the verb, 遅い (late, slow) is the adjective.

choices.text: {遅|おそ}いです。
choices.feedback: 遅い is an adjective ('slow / late'). Apologize: 遅れてすみません.
choices.why: Use the verb 遅れる for 'to be late': 遅れてすみません.

choices.text: ごめんね！
choices.feedback: ごめんね is for friends. With a teacher, use すみません.
choices.why: Match apologies to the relationship: ごめん (friends), すみません (polite), 申し訳ありません (formal).

challenges.title: A compliment
challenges.context: Your classmate Mika notices your new jacket.

steps.speaker: mika
steps.text: その{服|ふく}、かわいいね！

choices.text: ほんと？ありがとう！
choices.feedback: A light, happy thank-you, in casual style to match hers.
choices.why: Casual compliments get casual thanks. ほんと？ adds a natural, modest touch.

choices.text: はい、かわいいです。
choices.feedback: Fully agreeing sounds a little boastful. A modest thank-you feels more natural.
choices.why: In Japanese it's common to receive compliments modestly (ほんと？／ありがとう) rather than agreeing outright.

choices.text: いいえ、{服|ふく}です。
choices.feedback: That doesn't respond to the compliment.
choices.why: React to compliments with ありがとう or a modest ほんと？／そうかな.

challenges.title: Take a photo?
challenges.context: You're at a temple and want someone to take your picture.

choices.text: すみません、{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}っていただけませんか？
choices.reading: Sumimasen, shashin o totte itadakemasen ka?
choices.translation: Excuse me, could you take a photo for me?
choices.feedback: 〜ていただけませんか is a very polite request. Perfect for a stranger.
choices.why: 〜ていただけませんか ('could I humbly receive you doing ~?') is one of the politest ways to ask a favour.

choices.text: {写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}りますか？
choices.feedback: That sounds like you're offering, or just asking about his plans.
choices.why: To ask a favour, use the te-form + ください／いただけませんか, not a plain question.

choices.text: {写真|しゃしん}をなくしました。
choices.feedback: That reports a lost photo!
choices.why: Choose the verb for what you want: 撮る (take a photo), なくす (lose).

challenges.title: Small talk
challenges.context: Your neighbour Mr. Mori greets you on a sweltering morning.

steps.speaker: ojisan
steps.text: {今日|きょう}は{暑|あつ}いですね。

choices.text: そうですね。{本当|ほんとう}に{暑|あつ}いですね。
choices.reading: Sou desu ne. Hontou ni atsui desu ne.
choices.feedback: そうですね agrees, and echoing the topic keeps the chat going.
choices.why: 〜ですね invites agreement. Respond with そうですね and add a little of your own.

choices.text: はい。
choices.feedback: Fine, but そうですね is the natural way to agree with 〜ですね.
choices.why: はい sounds like answering a factual question. そうですね shares the feeling.

choices.text: いいえ、{暑|あつ}いです。
choices.feedback: いいえ disagrees, then you agreed. That's confusing!
choices.why: If you agree, start with そうですね. If you don't, say そうですか？ softly.

challenges.title: Trying clothes
challenges.context: You're in a clothing shop. The jacket you tried on is too big.

steps.speaker: hiro
steps.text: サイズはいかがですか？

choices.text: ちょっと{大|おお}きいです。{小|ちい}さいのはありますか？
choices.reading: Chotto ookii desu. Chiisai no wa arimasu ka?
choices.translation: It's a bit big. Do you have a smaller one?
choices.feedback: Clear problem + polite question. Adjective + の = 'a ~ one'.
choices.why: Adjective + の makes 'the ~ one' (小さいの = a small one). ちょっと softens the complaint.

choices.text: {小|ちい}さいをください。
choices.feedback: Close! Add の to make 'a small one': 小さいのをください.
choices.why: An adjective can't take を directly. Turn it into a noun with の: 小さいのをください.

choices.text: サイズです。
choices.feedback: That doesn't say how it fits.
choices.why: Describe the fit with an adjective: 大きい (big), 小さい (small), ちょうどいい (just right).

challenges.title: Booking by phone
challenges.context: You call a restaurant to book a table for Friday.

steps.speaker: hiro
steps.text: はい、さくら{食堂|しょくどう}でございます。

choices.text: もしもし、{予約|よやく}をお{願|ねが}いしたいんですが…
choices.reading: Moshimoshi, yoyaku o onegai shitai n desu ga…
choices.translation: Hello, I'd like to make a reservation…
choices.feedback: 〜たいんですが… politely opens a request and lets them take over.
choices.why: Ending with んですが… (trailing off) is a soft, very natural way to start a request.

choices.text: {予約|よやく}！
choices.feedback: They'll understand, but one word sounds abrupt on the phone.
choices.why: Phone Japanese is extra polite. Use full sentences with お願いします.

choices.text: さくら{食堂|しょくどう}ですか？さようなら。
choices.feedback: You hung up before booking!
choices.why: Confirming you've reached the right place is fine, but then say what you want: 予約をお願いします.

challenges.title: Oops!
challenges.context: You accidentally bump into Mr. Mori on a crowded street.

choices.text: あ、すみません！{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}ですか？
choices.translation: Oh, I'm sorry! Are you okay?
choices.feedback: Apologize, then check on him. Kind and natural.
choices.why: すみません is the all-purpose apology with strangers. 大丈夫ですか？ shows care.

choices.text: ありがとうございます！
choices.feedback: That's 'thank you'. After bumping into someone, apologize.
choices.why: すみません covers both 'excuse me' and 'sorry'. ありがとう is only for thanks.

choices.text: ごめん。
choices.feedback: ごめん is casual. With an older stranger, すみません is better.
choices.why: Use polite apologies with people you don't know, especially older people.

challenges.title: Saying no nicely
challenges.context: Mika invites you out, but you have an exam tomorrow.

steps.speaker: mika
steps.text: {今夜|こんや}、ごはん{行|い}かない？

choices.text: ごめん、{今夜|こんや}はちょっと…また{今度|こんど}ね！
choices.reading: Gomen, kon'ya wa chotto… mata kondo ne!
choices.translation: Sorry, tonight's a bit… Next time!
choices.feedback: ちょっと… softly says no, and また今度 keeps the friendship warm.
choices.why: Japanese refusals are often indirect: 〜はちょっと… Adding また今度 suggests another time.

choices.text: いいえ、{行|い}きません。
choices.feedback: Clear, but it sounds cold. Soften it with ごめん and ちょっと….
choices.why: A flat いいえ + negative can feel harsh. Indirect refusals are kinder.

choices.text: はい、{行|い}きません。
choices.feedback: はい + 行きません mixes yes and no.
choices.why: Answering 〜ない？ invitations: うん／いいね (yes) or ごめん、ちょっと… (no).

challenges.title: Hotel check-in
challenges.context: You arrive at a hotel front desk.

steps.speaker: hiro
steps.text: いらっしゃいませ。お{名前|なまえ}をお{願|ねが}いします。

choices.text: スミスです。{予約|よやく}しています。
choices.translation: I'm Smith. I have a reservation.
choices.feedback: Name + です and your booking status. Clear and polite.
choices.why: 〜しています describes a current state: 予約しています = 'I have (made) a booking'.

choices.text: お{名前|なまえ}はスミスです。
choices.feedback: お名前 is honorific. Never add お to your own name.
choices.why: Honorific お／ご are for other people's things. For yourself: 名前はスミスです, or just スミスです.

choices.text: {名前|なまえ}をください。
choices.feedback: You asked HIM for a name!
choices.why: When asked for information, give it: [name] です.

challenges.title: Dinner with a host family
challenges.context: Your host father, Mr. Mori, serves dinner.

steps.speaker: ojisan
steps.text: さあ、どうぞ{食|た}べてください。

choices.text: いただきます！
choices.translation: Let's eat! (Thank you for the food.)
choices.feedback: The set phrase before eating.
choices.why: いただきます is said before eating to thank everyone involved in the meal.

choices.text: ごちそうさまでした！
choices.translation: Thank you for the meal! (after eating)
choices.feedback: That's said AFTER eating. You haven't started yet!
choices.why: Before eating: いただきます. After eating: ごちそうさまでした.

choices.text: {食|た}べてください。
choices.feedback: You repeated his invitation back to him.
choices.why: Respond to an invitation to eat with いただきます.

choices.text: はい、とてもおいしかったです。ごちそうさまでした！
choices.reading: Hai, totemo oishikatta desu. Gochisousama deshita!
choices.translation: Yes, it was delicious. Thank you for the meal!
choices.feedback: Past tense for a finished meal, plus the closing phrase.
choices.why: おいしい → おいしかった (past tense of い-adjectives: drop い, add かった).

choices.text: はい、おいしいです。
choices.feedback: Kind! But the meal's finished, so the past tense おいしかった fits better.
choices.why: い-adjectives take a past tense: おいしい → おいしかった.

choices.text: いいえ、おいしかったです。
choices.feedback: いいえ (no) followed by praise is confusing!
choices.why: Start with はい when you agree.
